# ledger_user_password (Resource)

Sets the password of a Ledger user. The password is **write-only**: it is read from the configuration when the password is set, and is never stored in the plan or the state (needs Terraform 1.11 or later). Because it is not stored, Terraform cannot see a password changed elsewhere; to set a new one, change the value **and** raise `password_wo_version`.

Setting a password ends every session of that user and revokes their device cookies. **With an API token this needs the root token of the root account**, even for the token owner's own password; any other token is refused with `root_token_required`. Ledger has no operation to remove a password, so destroying this resource only forgets it: the password stays set. Disable the user (destroy `ledger_user`) to stop sign-in. Ledger enforces a minimum length (configured on the server, in bytes) and at most 1024 bytes, with no composition rules.

Not importable: there is nothing to read back.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# The password is write-only: read from the configuration when it is set, never stored in the plan or the state.
# Needs Terraform 1.11 or later and the root token of the root account. Supply the value from an ephemeral source.
variable "alex_password" {
  type      = string
  sensitive = true
  ephemeral = true
}

resource "ledger_user_password" "reader" {
  user_id     = ledger_user.reader.id
  password_wo = var.alex_password

  # Raise this number to set the password again (changing password_wo alone does nothing).
  password_wo_version = 1
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

> **NOTE**: [Write-only arguments](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments) are supported in Terraform 1.11 and later.

- `password_wo` (String, Sensitive, [Write-only](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/resources/ephemeral#write-only-arguments)) The new password. Write-only: never stored in the plan or the state, and not shown. Supply it from an ephemeral source, not a literal checked into version control. A change to this value alone does nothing; raise `password_wo_version` to apply it.
- `user_id` (String) The Ledger identifier of the user. Changing it sets the password of the other user (the resource is replaced).

### Optional

- `password_wo_version` (Number) A number you raise to set the password again. Terraform stores it (it is not secret) and calls Ledger when it changes.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The identifier of the user (the same as `user_id`).
- `sessions_ended` (Number) How many sessions the last password change ended.
